uncited: This family defines the geometric intersection between a camera ray and 3D Gaussian splats, which are ellipsoidal primitives used in novel view synthesis.
It solves the problem of accurately determining which splats contribute to a pixel and at what depth, enabling alpha blending and depth-based operations.

It distinguishes itself from sibling methods by handling the specific quadratic nature of Gaussian density fields, supporting both exact ellipsoid intersection and numerical stabilization for degenerate cases, unlike [Sphere Intersection](1620-sphere-intersection.md) which assumes constant radius or [Ray-Triangle Intersection](11312-ray-triangle-intersection.md) which handles planar surfaces.
The concept of ray-splat intersection evolved from the need to render 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) efficiently in real-time.
Standard 3DGS uses a rasterization-based approach that approximates the projection of Gaussians onto the image plane.
